(henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.1460/2013 vide its judgment and award dated 21.04.2017.

The appellants herein shall henceforth be referred to as 'claimants' and respondent Nos.1 and 2 shall henceforth be referred to as 'owner' and 'insurer' of the lorry bearing registration No.HR-55/M-4686.
3.
The claimants are the legal representatives of the deceased Ramachandra Gurulingappa Navi (for short, 'Ramachandra').

The claim petition discloses that on 28.07.2013 at about 2.30 p.m., the said Ramachandra was riding pillion on a motorcycle bearing registration NC: 2023:KHC-K:1448 No.KA-04/EG-9498 (henceforth referred to as the 'motorcycle') from Halagunaki to Ballolli and when he along with the rider of the motorcycle reached near Gundwan bus stand on Zalaki - Horti road, driver of the lorry bearing registration No.HR-55/M-4686 (henceforth referred to as 'lorry')
drove it in a rash and negligent manner from the opposite direction and dashed against the motorcycle.
As a result, the rider of the motorcycle as well as the pillion rider sustained fatal injuries and succumbed to it at the spot.
The claimants claimed that the deceased Ramachandra was a driver and was earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month and contributed all his income to the maintenance and upkeep of the family.
They, therefore, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the owner and insurer of the lorry.
4. Though the owner of the lorry was served with notice, he did not choose to appear before the Tribunal and hence, was placed ex parte.
The insurer of the lorry contested the claim petition and contended that the rider of the motorcycle was rash and negligent as he came from the wrong side and dashed against the lorry.

It contended that the jurisdictional Police after conducting an investigation filed an abated charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle and a charge sheet against the driver of the lorry, indicating that the rider of the motorcycle and the driver of the lorry were equally negligent and contributed to the accident.

In addition, it contended that the driver of the lorry did not possess a valid licence and therefore, there was breach of the terms of policy of insurance and hence, it was exempted from the liability to pay the compensation claimed by the claimants.
6. Based on these contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.2 was examined as PW.2 and a witness was examined as PW.3 and documents were marked.

The insurer examined one of its NC: 2023:KHC-K:1448 officers as RW.1 and marked a copy of insurance policy as Ex.R1 and five other documents as Exs.R2 to R6.
7.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the driver of the lorry as well as the rider of the motorcycle were equally negligent and contributed to the accident.

In so far as the quantum of compensation to which the claimants were entitled to, the Tribunal considered the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month and did not factor loss of future prospects and considered the age of the deceased as 55 years based on Ex.P5, copy of post mortem report and deducted 1/3rd towards his personal and living expenses awarded the following compensation:

The Tribunal held that since the deceased rider of the motorcycle and the driver of the lorry were equally negligent in causing the accident, 50% of the compensation amount had to be deducted and consequently, it held that the claimants in MVC No.1460/2013 were entitled to compensation of Rs.4,64,500/- along with interest at 9% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization and directed the insurer of the lorry to pay the compensation of Rs.4,64,500/- along with interest as stated above.
8. Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants have filed this appeal.
9.

Learned counsel for the claimants contended that the deceased was a driver and he was earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month and therefore, the Tribunal must have considered the income at a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month.

He also contends that if loss of future prospects is considered at 10%
of the notional income, then the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1448 notional income of the deceased for the purpose of determination of loss of dependency ought to have been considered at Rs.11,000/- and consequently, the compensation deserves to be enhanced.
He also contended that the Tribunal failed to award just compensation under the conventional heads.

10. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer / respondent No.2 contended that the notional income of a person who died or who was injured in a road traffic accident in the year 2013 was considered at a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month.

He submitted that the claimants did not produce any records to show that the deceased was a qualified driver and therefore, the assessment of the notional income of the deceased by the Tribunal at Rs.8,000/- per month was not warranted and therefore, the claimants are not entitled for any enhancement of compensation.

He further submits that the Tribunal while granting compensation had awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium and a - 10 - Shantabai And Ors vs Arti Jain And Anr on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144112439/
5 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1448 sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of love and affection and the same being excessive deserves to be modified and sought that just compensation be awarded.

sentences.text: 11. I have considered the contentions of the learned counsel for the claimants and the learned counsel for the insurer.
I have perused the records of the Tribunal as well as its Judgment and Award.

12. It is seen that the insurer has contested the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the ground that the compensation awarded towards loss of spousal consortium and loss of love and affection was excessive.

However, the Tribunal having held that the notional income of the deceased was Rs.8,000/- per month must have awarded loss of future prospects at 10% as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LTD. v. PRANAY SETHI [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LTD. v. PRANAY SETHI [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, what needs to be considered is that the Tribunal had awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium and a - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1448 sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss love and affection, which at any rate was excessive.
Consequently, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not warrant any enhancement.
13. Hence, this appeal lacks merit and is dismissed.
The impugned Judgment and Award dated 21.04.2017 passed by the IV Additional District Judge and Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-XIII, Vijayapura, in MVC No.1460/2013 is confirmed.

14. Since the claimant was a pillion rider, he is entitled to recover the entire compensation awarded by the Tribunal from either the owner of the motorcycle or respondent No.2, the insurer of the lorry bearing registration No.HR-55/M-4686 in accordance with law.

In the event the compensation is recovered from the insurer, the insurer is entitled to recover 50% of the compensation from the owner of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-04/EG-9498 in accordance with law.

This appeal is filed by the claimants challenging the finding regarding the negligence of the deceased and the quantum of compensation awarded by the IV Additional District Judge and Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-XIII, Vijayapura, (henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.1462/2013 vide its judgment and award dated 21.04.2017.

24. Being aggrieved by the finding of the Tribunal regarding negligence as well as the quantum of compensation determined by the Tribunal, the present appeal is filed.
25. Learned counsel for the claimants contended that the deceased was neither negligent nor had contributed to the accident and there is no evidence to establish that the deceased was negligent.

He relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Khenyei v. New India Assurance Company Limited and Others [(2015) 9 SCC 273] and contended that the finding regarding contributory negligence cannot be handed down unless there is acceptable evidence adduced by the insurer.

He contends that the deceased who was riding the motorcycle ought to have exercised caution and must have remained within his lane and could not have wandered into the right lane.

He, therefore, submitted that the finding of the Tribunal that both the rider of the motorcycle and driver of the lorry were negligent and contributed to the accident is just and proper and therefore, the finding of the Tribunal regarding negligence need not be interfered with.
27. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.
The fact that the motorcycle and the lorry met with an accident in a head on collision is not much in dispute.
Both the rider and the pillion rider died in the accident.
It is seen that the accident happened at 2.30 p.m. on 28.07.2013 on a road which measured 40 feet wide.
The only document available on record is Ex.P3 which was a document drawn by the jurisdictional Police by visiting the spot.
This document discloses that the deceased had ridden the motorcycle on the extreme right side of the road and dashed against the lorry driven from the opposite direction.
There is no explanation as to how and why the deceased wandered on to the right side of the road.
If the deceased had strayed on to the right side and dashed against lorry, it cannot be said that the deceased was not negligent and was not responsible for the accident.
In that view of the matter, the finding of the Tribunal that the deceased was negligent and had contributed to the accident
cannot be interfered with and hence, the finding of the Tribunal regarding negligence is proper and correct.

In so far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the deceased was aged 50 years as on the date of the accident and the Tribunal failed to factor loss of future prospects at 10% of the notional income of the deceased as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. V. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

However, since the Tribunal has granted compensation of Rs.10,03,000/-, this Court does not find any justification for enhancement of the compensation.

of the compensation and held that the claimants were entitled to Rs.5,01,500/- along with interest at 9% per annum from the date of the clam petition till the date of realization.
opennyai_summary.decision:
13. Hence, this appeal lacks merit and is dismissed.
However, the Tribunal has granted Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium and a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of loss of love and affection and a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of care and guidance of the minor child i.e,
claimant No.3 and interest at 9% per annum which was at any rate excessive and even if the loss of dependency is considered by factoring loss of future prospects at 10% of the notional income of the deceased, the compensation would not exceed a sum of Rs.10,00,000/-.
However, since the Tribunal has granted compensation of Rs.10,03,000/-, this Court does not find any justification for enhancement of the compensation.
Hence, this appeal lacks merit and same is dismissed.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
He relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Khenyei v. New India Assurance Company Limited and Others [(2015) 9 SCC 273] and contended that the finding regarding contributory negligence cannot be handed down unless there is acceptable evidence adduced by the insurer.
He, therefore, submitted that the finding of the Tribunal that both the rider of the motorcycle and driver of the lorry were negligent and contributed to the accident is just and proper and therefore, the finding of the Tribunal regarding negligence need not be interfered with.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There is no explanation as to how and why the deceased wandered on to the right side of the road.
If the deceased had strayed on to the right side and dashed against lorry, it cannot be said that the deceased was not negligent and was not responsible for the accident.
In that view of the matter, the finding of the Tribunal that the deceased was negligent and had contributed to the accident
cannot be interfered with and hence, the finding of the Tribunal regarding negligence is proper and correct.
In so far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the deceased was aged 50 years as on the date of the accident and the Tribunal failed to factor loss of future prospects at 10% of the notional income of the deceased as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. V. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].
